background.fact: PGM means Portable Gray Map and stores grayscale pixels.
Raw PGM begins with P5 and stores samples in binary form.
Plain PGM begins with P2 and represents samples as decimal text.
A Maxval above 255 requires two bytes for each raw sample.
The conventional media type is image/x-portable-graymap; IANA has not registered it.
Netpbm also uses PGM for opacity masks, with a different interpretation of sample values.

windows.note: Reads and writes the PGM member of the Netpbm family.
Provides programs and libnetpbm for processing graymaps.

mac.note: Reads and writes the PGM member of the Netpbm family.
Provides programs and libnetpbm for processing graymaps.

linux.note: Reads and writes the PGM member of the Netpbm family.
Provides programs and libnetpbm for processing graymaps.

problems.fact: Older readers may reject samples deeper than eight bits; pamdepth can reduce Maxval.
Some readers stop after the first image even though raw PGM permits a sequence.
Linear-light and sRGB variants can display differently from the specified BT.709 interpretation.

background.fact: Microsoft and Adobe developed OpenType by extending TrueType.
OpenType 1.0 was published in 1997.
OpenType files organize glyph and text-layout data into tables.
Glyph descriptions may use TrueType outlines, CFF outlines, bitmaps, or SVG.
The registered media type is font/otf.
OpenType variation tables allow several related faces within one font resource.

windows.note: Opens .otf fonts for inspection and editing.
Reads binary OTF tables and writes an XML representation for inspection.

mac.note: Installs and validates OpenType and OpenType-SVG fonts.
Includes OTF in its Open dialog.
Reads binary OTF tables and writes an XML representation for inspection.

linux.note: Opens OTF files through its File menu.
Reads binary OTF tables and writes an XML representation for inspection.

problems.fact: An older rendering engine may lack support for a font's particular outline representation.
A corrupt font can prevent correct display; Font Book provides file validation.
Duplicate installed copies can cause conflicts; Font Book can resolve duplicates.

background.fact: Sun's published AU specification describes a fixed header, an annotation area, and audio samples.
AU starts with the four-byte signature .snd.
The header records the encoding, sample rate, and channel count.
Multibyte header and sample values use big-endian ordering.
Defined encodings include linear PCM, mu-law, A-law, floating point, and ADPCM.
FFmpeg uses audio/basic as the media label for its Sun AU writer.
The IANA audio/basic definition describes mono eight-bit mu-law at 8 kHz; it is narrower than the full set of AU encodings.

windows.note: Imports AU audio without adding the optional FFmpeg library.
Reads supported NeXT/Sun encodings using Read from file.

mac.note: Imports AU audio without adding the optional FFmpeg library.
Reads supported NeXT/Sun encodings using Read from file.

linux.note: Imports AU audio without adding the optional FFmpeg library.
Reads supported NeXT/Sun encodings using Read from file.

problems.fact: Old Audacity projects need their associated audio files in the expected locations.
An isolated Audacity block does not supply the arrangement stored by the AUP project.
Praat's Sun export quantizes samples to 16-bit mono; keep amplitudes below one to avoid clipping.
More than two interleaved channels are allowed by the specification, but some applications cannot handle them.

background.fact: Fujifilm identifies RAF as its original camera RAW format.
The X-T3 can record either uncompressed or losslessly compressed RAF data.
Lossless RAW compression uses a reversible algorithm.
RAW+JPEG recording saves a ready-to-use JPEG alongside the RAW capture.
Fujifilm's RAW converter develops RAF data recorded by X-series cameras.
Film Simulation can be applied during RAW development in Fujifilm's converter.

windows.app: RAW FILE CONVERTER EX powered by SILKYPIX
windows.note: Fujifilm offers RAW development software; check its camera compatibility list.
Uses a connected compatible camera's image processor for RAW conversion.
Lists RAF as a readable camera RAW format.

mac.app: RAW FILE CONVERTER EX powered by SILKYPIX
mac.note: Fujifilm offers RAW development software; check its camera compatibility list.
Uses a connected compatible camera's image processor for RAW conversion.
Lists RAF as a readable camera RAW format.

linux.note: Recognizes RAF for import; camera support comes from its RawSpeed library.

problems.fact: Losslessly compressed RAF needs software that understands that RAW variant.
X RAW STUDIO requires a supported camera connection; it does not perform the conversion with the computer CPU.
New camera models can require a converter update; Fujifilm publishes model support additions.

background.fact: XLSX is Microsoft Excel's XML workbook format used from Excel 2007.
Its content is a ZIP package of Open Packaging Conventions parts.
Several parts in that package are XML documents.
XLSX cannot store VBA code or Excel 4.0 macro sheets.
Its registered media type is application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet.

windows.note: Opens Excel workbook formats; check imported features before resaving.
Opens the workbook through File > Open.

mac.note: Reads Excel spreadsheets.
Imports .xls and .xlsx spreadsheets for editing.
Reads Excel workbook files.

linux.note: Imports both legacy binary and Open XML Excel workbooks.
Its manual documents Excel and Office Open XML import support.

web.note: Imports Excel files or edits Office files in Drive.
Opens XLSX directly; opening legacy XLS converts a working copy to XLSX.

mobile.app: Microsoft Excel for Android and iOS
mobile.note: XLSX can be edited; legacy XLS opens read-only.

problems.fact: Saving a workbook with macros as XLSX cannot retain its VBA code; use a macro-enabled format.
Exporting a workbook to CSV saves only the active worksheet and discards formatting.
Google recommends retaining Excel for datasets above its stated Sheets cell limit or unusual chart types.

background.fact: XLS identifies several generations of Microsoft Excel binary workbooks.
The Excel 97–2003 workbook uses BIFF8.
Excel 5.0/95 used the BIFF5 variant with the same .xls ending.
Modern Excel opens Excel 97–2003 workbooks in Compatibility Mode.
The registered Excel media type is application/vnd.ms-excel.

windows.note: Opens Excel workbook formats; check imported features before resaving.
Opens the workbook through File > Open.

mac.note: Reads Excel spreadsheets.
Imports .xls and .xlsx spreadsheets for editing.
Reads Excel workbook files.

linux.note: Imports both legacy binary and Open XML Excel workbooks.
Its manual documents Excel and Office Open XML import support.

web.note: Imports Excel files or edits Office files in Drive.
Opens XLSX directly; opening legacy XLS converts a working copy to XLSX.

mobile.app: Microsoft Excel for Android and iOS
mobile.note: XLSX can be edited; legacy XLS opens read-only.

problems.fact: Modern worksheet features can be lost when a workbook is saved as Excel 97–2003.
An XLS destination cannot hold cells outside its older row and column limits.
Text-format exports lose workbook formatting and keep only the active sheet.

background.fact: Adobe documents F4V among files derived from the MPEG-4 container structure.
F4V is a container rather than the H.264 video codec itself.
Adobe's playback API accepts H.264 video and HE-AAC v2 audio in these files.
Adobe AIR and Flash Player 9.0.115.0 added the documented MPEG-4-family playback support.
F4V playback can deliver metadata and cue-point events.
Flash Player support ended in 2020; browser Flash is no longer a current playback method.

windows.note: Its MOV-family demuxer explicitly recognizes the .f4v extension.
Reads MP4/MOV containers and decodes H.264 and AAC; test the particular F4V file.

mac.note: Its MOV-family demuxer explicitly recognizes the .f4v extension.
Reads MP4/MOV containers and decodes H.264 and AAC; test the particular F4V file.

linux.note: Its MOV-family demuxer explicitly recognizes the .f4v extension.
Reads MP4/MOV containers and decodes H.264 and AAC; test the particular F4V file.

problems.fact: An old Flash embed can stop working because Adobe blocked Flash Player content after its retirement.
The archived Adobe player API supports the documented codec combinations, not every stream a container might hold.
Some AIR iOS playback APIs omit metadata and cue-point events available elsewhere.

background.fact: DivX video files belong to DivX's video playback and authoring ecosystem.
VideoLAN lists DivX versions one through six among its supported video compression formats.
DivX authoring can add menus and chapter points to a movie.
A DivX movie can contain subtitles and more than one audio track.
DivX certification profiles distinguish device playback capabilities.
The .divx extension is one of the formats explicitly listed by DivX Player.

windows.note: Decodes the documented DivX video formats.
Plays DIVX files and offers soundtrack selection.

mac.note: Provides DivX decoding on the Mac.
The vendor offers its player on macOS.

linux.note: FFmpeg's test player handles DivX streams and subtitle samples; menus are not promised.

problems.fact: Advanced menus, chapters, and tracks depend on the receiving device's DivX profile.
DivX is primarily a delivery format; Adobe advises conversion before Premiere editing.
Having a DivX video decoder does not by itself establish support for every advanced authoring feature.

background.fact: XPS means XML Paper Specification and is used for electronic documents and printing.
The format uses XML and Open Packaging Conventions.
XPS fixes page layout instead of reflowing the content.
Its document structure includes ordered fixed documents and fixed pages.
Font resources can be embedded in an XPS document.
Its registered media type is application/vnd.ms-xpsdocument.

windows.note: Free Windows reader with XPS support.
Lists XPS among its document handlers.
Its documented supported formats include XPS.

mac.note: Its documented supported formats include XPS.
Reads XPS pages for rendering or text extraction.

linux.note: Views XPS through its document handler.
Its documented supported formats include XPS.

problems.fact: XPS page descriptions are not the editable source document; retain the original authoring file.
Viewer features differ by format; do not assume PDF annotations or forms also work in XPS.
A changed signed document can be detected by XPS signature verification.
